version_guard.provenance: All four guarded probes ran against concrete Claude Code 2.1.330 on 2026-11-22; each ended version-guard: verdict=single-version start=2.1.330 end=2.1.330. Arm S observed concurrent hook execution in 12/12 event pairs with relay-first in 3/12. Arm D completed 5/5 explicit-deny runs with every run exiting 0 and firing exactly one Stop, all 5 verifying an errored Bash result. Arm T killed all 8 overrun firings while all 4 sessions exited 0 with replies at 5.1 s after Stop-hook start. The dedicated TUI probe observed one Stop per turn at 12.1 s / 2.1 s. The allowed-tool probe hit the documented zero-firing driver window on both prompts (205.1 s each, zero firings). probe-claude-contracts T2 completed both turns with two Stops per turn for two loaded sources (49.0 s / 32.0 s). A same-session authenticated claude-print stream-json PTY capture used the same pinned binary; its 34-record stdout was byte-identical to the transcript, with no result, CR, or blank records. The sanitized family uses representatives from that live capture (a live thinking + text split assistant pair; no live ai-title records this run — the retained forwarding case is re-versioned) and retains historical framing cases. Envelope deltas new versus the 2.1.327 sample: the environment attachment's snapshot dropped scratchpadDirectory, api-request-shape's shape field became an object (system texts plus tool objects), and api-request-blob's message field became an object (role plus content blocks); the live cost-state records carried a single claude-sonnet-4-6 modelUsage entry with hasUnknownModelCost false. Replay bytes and error objects were produced and verified against the production reader and emitter.

notes.isolation: Every probe ran with HOME redirected into a throwaway sandbox; the host real settings and .claude.json were not read or modified. The host credentials file, when present, was copied file-to-file into the sandbox and never printed.
notes.cross_source_order_evidence: 2.1.330 Arm S: across six runs and both hook events, all 12/12 pairs were concurrent; the relay started first in 3/12. The result is concurrency, not a contractual source order: claude-print must not depend on order.
notes.tui_per_turn_evidence: The dedicated probe-tui-second-turn.sh run on 2.1.330 completed two TUI turns: turn 1 fired 1 Stop with its reply rendered in 12.1 s, and turn 2 fired 1 Stop with its reply rendered in 2.1 s. The allowed-tool TUI arm hit the documented zero-firing driver window on both prompts (205.1 s each, zero firings).
notes.degraded_path_hazard: Arm D on 2.1.330: 5 of 5 explicit-deny runs verified an errored Bash result, every run exited 0 and fired exactly one Stop. The historical 2.1.270 extra-Stop hazard did not reproduce.
notes.print_mode_tool_use_evidence: Arm P on 2.1.330 used --allowedTools=Bash. Both sequential Bash rounds completed in order, the final message was DONE, exit was 0, and exactly 1 Stop fired.
notes.cutoff_evidence: The focused 2.1.330 -p run with --max-turns 2 exited 1 and fired zero own Stops; the cutoff remains owned by the --stop-hook-timeout watchdog, not the Stop Poller.
notes.hook_timeout_evidence: Arm T on 2.1.330 configured a relay-position hook with timeout 5 s and sleep 30 s across four real single-turn runs: all 8 event firings were killed, all 4 sessions exited 0 with replies, and each Stop hook-to-process completion was 5.1 s.
